data.source_text_main_point: The Supreme Court's upcoming ruling in MGM v. Grokster will determine whether software companies can be held legally responsible for copyright infringement by users of peer-to-peer technology, a decision that could either affirm the legality of such networks or overturn the precedent set by the 1984 Betamax case, thereby impacting billions in future revenues.

actors.name: Sony Corp. v. Universal City Studios

statements.key_statement: The MGM v. Grokster ruling will decide whether to uphold or overturn the 1984 Betamax precedent, a choice that could determine billions in future revenues for the home video market.
statements.long_statement: The outcome of the MGM v. Grokster litigation will determine whether the United States legal system will uphold the 1984 Betamax precedent, which protects technology manufacturers, or overturn it to impose liability on software creators for unauthorized copying by their users. This judicial decision is critical because it stands to redefine the economic viability of the home video market, with billions of dollars in future revenues now hanging in the balance depending on whether the court affirms or rejects the established legal standard for peer-to-peer technology.
